title: CI auto-fix, split view and scheduled tasks, with the reviewer's seven findings fixed
request: The owner's goal: the same capabilities as Claude Code desktop; the side-by-side's medium gaps.
plan: CI auto-fix on a session's pull request

decisions.decision: the app pushes the fix, not the agent
decisions.why: the push stays one audited act of the app, after checks only it can make

decisions.decision: push only a fix turn that ended on its own, untouched
decisions.why: a stop, an error, a restart or the person's message means the commit is not a finished fix

decisions.decision: split view embeds the same page; frame-ancestors 'self'
decisions.why: each side keeps all its behaviour with no new state; no other site can frame the app

decisions.decision: a scheduled run gets its own copy in a git project
decisions.why: it never edits files the person is working on

change: dclab-code server/ci_fix.js and server/schedules.js (new), server/app.js, server/engine.js (send and outcome take 'app' as the sender), server/events.js and server/transcript.js (an app message said as the app's), server/git.js (headSha), server/worktree.js (headRefOid), web/* (CI switch, split pane, scheduled tasks section, keys off in a split), tests, docs.

findings.defect: a stopped, failed or interrupted fix turn was still pushed
findings.scenario: the person presses Stop mid-fix: the next look pushed the half-done commit (verified)
findings.cause: 'fixing' was cleared only by the push
findings.fix: push only when an app message was followed by a successful result with no stop and no other message
findings.test: server test: Stop mid-fix, nothing pushed; undoing the check fails it

findings.defect: an unattended fix turn ran in a session whose project (and guards) were removed
findings.scenario: auto-fix on, project removed from the list
findings.cause: the tick called send directly, past the route's check

findings.defect: the app's own acts were recorded as the person's
findings.scenario: ci_fix_started and ci_fix_pushed by: person, a false label in R&D's sets
findings.fix: outcome takes a sender; the app's acts are 'app'
findings.test: server test checks every ci_fix outcome

findings.defect: check names from CI reached the agent unchanged
findings.scenario: a check named with new lines and an instruction
findings.fix: one line, short, no control characters; marked as data; never in bypass mode
findings.test: server test with an injected name

findings.defect: the auto-fix switch had no same-page check
findings.scenario: a local script with the token turned it on as the person

findings.defect: the tick ignored a busy copy
findings.scenario: a fix turn during the person's merge or push
findings.fix: wait while merging, pushing, removing or being made

findings.defect: Y/N/A in a split answered the card of whichever side had focus
findings.scenario: focus in the right pane, the person means the left card
findings.fix: the keys are off in a split view

findings.defect: a scheduled task could run twice in one slot
findings.scenario: the run recorded the system clock, not the slot's time
findings.test: server test 'never twice in one slot'

findings.defect: the copy could hold commits not on the pull request when a fix starts
findings.scenario: the person committed in the copy without pushing
findings.cause: no check of HEAD against the PR head

measurements.name: tests
measurements.gate: every test passes; the untouched-turn check's test fails when it is undone
measurements.result: dclab-code 129 of 129; without the check the half-done commit is pushed and the test fails

outcome: DCLab Code fixes failing CI on its own within strict limits, shows two sessions side by side, and runs scheduled tasks.
lessons: An unattended action needs proof that the work it ships is finished, not just a flag set when it started.
Every record the app writes for itself must say it is the app's, or training learns a false label.
risks: CI logs remain untrusted input to an unattended turn (asks still apply); review comments, merge conflicts and auto-merge are not handled
